messages:
Ben (Recruiter): Heads-up  contractor (Maya L.) converting to FTE 01/06. Manager asked if remaining contractor sick allowance (3 days) can be carried into her new sick balance. Any blockers?

Nora (People Ops): Hi! Not standard since contractors don't live in our accrual system, but we approve documented one-offs. Need contract clause + manager approval + payroll check for tax treatment.

Ilya (Manager): We paid those 3 days as part of monthly stipend. Ilya approves converting 3 days into Maya's sick bank on start date.

Tara (HRBP): Confirmed: process is allowed as BENEFIT_CONVERSION exception. Steps: (1) attach contract to employee record, (2) manager approval in thread, (3) create exception EXC-2024-420, (4) add one-time 3-day credit on 01/06, (5) notify payroll. Note: don't change accrual rates.

Payroll Bot: FYI payroll needs documentation; retroactive payments or credits could be taxable. Please open payroll ticket PL-10012 with contract attached.

PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: exceptions must be logged. Use exception type BENEFIT_CONVERSION and include evidence link. See policy: https://redwood.example/hr/policies/benefit-conversions

Ben (Recruiter): Contract snippet uploaded to employee docs. Ilya, can you post a one-line approval for records?

Ilya (Manager): approve conversion of 3 contracted sick days to company sick bank for Maya L. on 2025-01-06.

Nora (People Ops): Thanks. Filing EXC-2024-420 and creating payroll ticket PL-10012. I'll schedule the HRIS grant for 2025-01-06 and add note: "Contract-to-FTE sick carryover approved by manager; EXC-2024-420". Closing loop unless payroll flags tax concern. :white_check_mark:
